headline.text: Free Gemini users lose Flash and Pro

slides.altText: Free Gemini users lose Flash and Pro

body.text: Gemini app users without a Google AI subscription will be limited to 3.5 Flash-Lite, the lightest tier. 3.6 Flash and 3.1 Pro will no longer be available to them.

slides.numberNote: Date free users lose Flash and Pro in the Gemini app

headline.text: AI Plus subscribers lose Pro too

slides.altText: AI Plus subscribers lose Pro too

body.text: AI Plus ($4.99 a month) will be limited to Flash-Lite and Flash, losing Pro, the most advanced tier. Google will email subscribers about when the change takes effect, so there is no fixed date.
9to5Google reports AI Pro and AI Ultra see no regressions, and AI Pro subscribers get Deep Think, Gemini's maximum parallel reasoning option, which is currently only on the two Ultra plans.

headline.text: One outlet says more models are going. Unconfirmed

slides.altText: One outlet says more models are going. Unconfirmed

body.text: NPowerUser says Google is retiring 3.6 and 3.7 Flash and has pulled dedicated Fast modes. Google's API deprecations page, updated Oct 1, lists no shutdown date for either. No other source confirms the claim.

headline.text: Gemini 4 Argon is announced, not widely out

slides.altText: Gemini 4 Argon is announced, not widely out

body.text: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon on Sept 30, first for trusted cyber defenders. Google says paid API customers and AI Ultra subscribers are next. 9to5Google says Argon's place in the Gemini app is unclear.

caption:
Google will limit Gemini app users without a paid plan to its Flash-Lite model starting Oct 9, and they will lose access to Flash and Pro. AI Plus subscribers lose Pro too, on a date Google will give them by email.

Flash-Lite is the lightest and fastest of Gemini's three model tiers, Flash is the middle option and Pro is the most advanced. Google is also adding low, medium and high effort levels, which make a model more capable on tasks but use more of your usage limit. 9to5Google reports AI Pro subscribers get Deep Think. NPowerUser says Google is retiring Gemini 3.6 and 3.7 Flash, but Google's API deprecations page and other sources don't confirm it. Gemini 4 Argon, announced Sept 30, is still in limited rollout.
